question: On a typical manual typewriter, what did pressing the shift key physically do?
options: It swapped in a second set of typebars
It raised the carriage or lowered the typebars
It turned each typebar's head halfway round
answer: It moved the carriage or the typebars. Each bar carried two letters on one slug, capital above small, and shift lifted the carriage or dropped the basket of bars so the other half struck. One bar per key halved the moving parts. Lifting a whole carriage was heavy work for a little finger.
move: When one part does two jobs, look for what moves to switch between them.
trap: Picturing capitals as a separate set of letters needing their own parts.
reference: Adler, The Writing Machine: A History of the Typewriter, Allen & Unwin, 1973
